_note: Claim-settlement rules for the compliance matrix. In India claim settlement is regulated nationally by IRDAI (and, for employee's compensation, by the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923), so every launch state gets the national rule for the product's line; there are no state-level claim-handling rules. Each rule was checked against the cited text on the date in 'verified' (see 'verified_url'); rules change, so Compliance must still confirm each launch state before go-live. A state entry under 'states' (none today) would override the national rule for that state.

default.source: IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024 (IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024, 5 September 2024), Part C: Retail General Insurance
default.citation: IRDAI Master Circular 2024, Part C, para V (processing and settlement of claims) and para VI (complaints, Insurance Ombudsman); IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
default.acknowledge_trigger: surveyor allocated within 24 hours of claim intimation, and the surveyor's details, role and duties sent to the insured immediately
default.decision_trigger: after the survey report is received, or after day 15 from surveyor allocation if that is earlier
default.extension_rule: No extension. The surveyor reports within 15 days of allocation; for each day the report is late, Rs 500 a day is payable to the claimant. Losses of Rs 50,000 or more (motor) or Rs 1 lakh or more (other lines) must be surveyed by a licensed surveyor and loss assessor. A claim not settled within these timelines carries interest at bank rate plus 2% from the date of intimation to the date of payment, paid without being asked. No claim may be rejected or closed for want of documents or for late intimation, or for a breach of warranty or condition unrelated to the loss. The decision timeline does not apply to property or building policies on reinstatement-value basis. The circular sets no separate payment deadline after the decision: enter the payment days from the insurer's board-approved claims policy. These timelines are set for retail policies; for commercial policies Compliance confirms the insurer's own claim turnaround times.

WorkersComp.source: Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, section 4A (compensation to be paid when due; penalty for default)
WorkersComp.citation: EC Act 1923 s.4A(1)-(3); s.19 (Commissioner decides disputes); IRDAI Master Circular 2024 para VI for the policyholder's grievance route

WorkersComp.extension_rule: No extension. Compensation falls due on the date of the accident (s.4A(1)). Where liability is disputed, the amount admitted is paid provisionally, to the Commissioner or the employee, without prejudice to the rest of the claim (s.4A(2)). If compensation is not paid within one month of falling due, the Commissioner must order simple interest at 12% a year and may add a penalty of up to 50% of the amount (s.4A(3)).
